To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the relaxivity of spin labeled polysubstituted polysaccharides is increased by 60% compared to the relaxivity of small hydrophilic nitroxides and that the spin labels are immobilized on the surface of the polysaccharide.

the spin labels bound to the polysaccharides are characterized by two distinct mobilities and that the relaxation rates of the spin labeled polysacarchides are enhanced compared to those of the small spin labeled molecules.

the relaxivity of polysubstituted nitroxyl spin labeled polysac-charides is enhanced by a factor 1.6 at 0.47T compared to that of small nitroxyl radicals and that the relaxation rate is dominated by the rotational motion of the spin labeled moieties.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis of polysubstituted dextrans and arabinogalanctans.
the synthesis and characterization of polysubstituted nitroxyl radicals, which are potential contrast media for magnetic resonance imaging.
the design of new magnetic resonance imaging agents based on polysaccharides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
polysaccharides are excellent carriers for spin labels and can be used as contrast agents in magnetic imaging.
spin labeled polysac-charides are potential contrast agents for MRI.
the spin label relaxation is dominated by the motion of the nitroxyl group.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
polysubstituted nitroxyl radicals are good candidates for magnetic resonance imaging contrast agents, but the molecular dynamics of these macromolecules is complex and requires further study.
the polysaccharide backbone is flexible and the spin labels are mobile.

the spin labeled polysac charides are potential contrast agents for MRI, but that the relaxivity is not as high as expected for such large molecules, which is due to the presence of a mobile fraction of spin labels.
The main takeaway from our work is that
spin labeled dextrans and arabinogaltactan are good candidates for MRI contrast agents, because their relaxivities are high, and they are biocompatible and biodegradable.

the polysaccharide backbone can be substituted without loss of mobility and that the resulting spin labeled macromolecules can serve as a model system for the study of the dynamics of spin labeled macromolecular contrast agents.
the spin labeled dextrans can be used as probes of the local environment and of the dynamics of the macromolecular chains.
